name: ICPC Square
description: ICPC Square is a hotel provided by the ICPC Committee for the accommodation of the participants. It consists of $$$N$$$ floors (numbered from $$$1$$$ to $$$N$$$). This hotel has a very unique elevator. If a person is currently at floor $$$x$$$, by riding the elevator once, they can go to floor $$$y$$$ if and only if $$$y$$$ is a multiple of $$$x$$$ and $$$y - x \leq D$$$. You are currently at floor $$$S$$$. You want to go to the highest possible floor by riding the elevator zero or more times. Determine the highest floor you can reach.
input_specification: A single line consisting of three integers $$$N$$$ $$$D$$$ $$$S$$$ ($$$2 \leq N \leq 10^{12}; 1 \leq D \leq N - 1; 1 \leq S \leq N$$$).
output_specification: Output a single integer representing the highest floor you can reach by riding the elevator zero or more times.
approach_summary: Precompute linear sieve to store minimum prime factor (spf[x]) up to N in O(N). Factorize any number x ≤ N in O(log x) steps.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 2045B — ICPC Square [242. Sieve, Prime Factorization and Divisors]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Every composite integer $X$ has at least one prime factor $\le \sqrt{X}$. Precomputing the Smallest Prime Factor (SPF) for all numbers up to $M$ via a linear sieve allows any $X \le M$ to be completely prime-factorized in $O(\log X)$ steps.
